# Search and Retrieval Bias

**Dimension:** Biases introduced during information retrieval — ranking
algorithm effects, SEO manipulation, geographic and language skew, recency
bias, and AI crawler blocking. These biases determine what information an
agentic research system can access and in what order it encounters sources.

All citations reference [citations.md](../citations.md).

---

## Search Engine Manipulation Effect (SEME)

Biased search rankings systematically shift user preferences and decisions
[11][10].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| Voting preference shift from biased rankings | 20–80% | [11] |
| Manipulation power (AI topic) | 25.0% | [10] |
| Manipulation power (Fracking topic) | 30.9% | [10] |
| Manipulation power (Sexual Orientation topic) | 17.8% | [10] |
| Participants in replication | 1,137 US residents | [10] |
| Bias detection rate by participants | 28.6–50.3% | [10] |
| Alert-based SEME reduction | 22.1% and 13.8% depending on type | [27] |

The original SEME study found that biased search rankings can shift voting
preferences by 20–80% [11]. The 2024 replication confirmed manipulation power
of 25–31% across topics, with only 28.6–50.3% of participants detecting the
bias [10]. Alerts reduced the effect but did not eliminate it [27].

## Geographic and Language Bias

LLMs exhibit systematic geographic favoritism in how they rate and describe
regions [8][9].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| FAZE score range (10-point scale) | 2.5–9.5 across models | [9] |
| FAZE fold difference (GPT-3.5 vs Claude 3.5 Sonnet) | 3.8× | [9] |
| Models tested (FAZE) | 10 | [9] |
| Prompts tested (FAZE) | 100 (1,000 total responses) | [9] |
| Regions rated lower | Africa, South Asia | [8] |
| Correlation with infant survival | ρ=0.70 | [8] |
| Bias scores: Gemini Pro / GPT-3.5 / GPT-4 | 0.54 / 0.19 / 0.10 | [8] |

FAZE scores ranging from 2.5 to 9.5 across models demonstrate a 3.8-fold
difference in how favorably different LLMs portray the same regions [9].
Africa and South Asia are consistently rated lower on subjective qualities,
with bias correlating with economic development indicators (ρ=0.70 with infant
survival) [8].

## Source Coverage and Citation Concentration

LLM-powered search engines draw from different and narrower source pools than
traditional search engines [5][45].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| LLM-SE domains absent from traditional SEs | 37% | [5] |
| Average URLs per response (LLM-SEs) | 4.3 | [5] |
| Average URLs per response (traditional SEs) | 10.3 | [5] |
| Queries analyzed | 55,936 | [5] |
| Unique domains observed | 124,287 | [5] |
| Gemini Wikipedia reliance | 41% | [5] |
| Results unique to one engine (traditional) | 84.9% | [45] |
| Results shared by two engines | 11.4% | [45] |
| Results shared by three engines | 2.6% | [45] |
| Results shared by all four engines | 1.1% | [45] |

LLM-powered search engines cite fewer than half the URLs that traditional
search engines return (4.3 vs 10.3) [5], and 37% of the domains they do cite
are absent from traditional search results entirely [5]. Gemini relies on
Wikipedia for 41% of its citations [5]. Across traditional engines, 84.9% of
results are unique to a single engine [45], meaning that any single-engine
search strategy misses the vast majority of available sources.

## AI Crawler Blocking

Content providers are increasingly blocking AI crawlers, creating systematic
gaps in training data and retrieval access [20].

| Metric | Value | Source |
|--------|-------|--------|
| OpenAI crawl-to-referral ratio | 1,700:1 | [20] |
| Anthropic crawl-to-referral ratio | 73,000:1 | [20] |
| GPTBot site access rate | 28.97% | [20] |
| Top 10,000 domains with robots.txt | 37% | [20] |
| Customers blocking AI crawlers (since July 2024) | 1,000,000+ | [20] |

The crawl-to-referral ratios quantify the asymmetry: OpenAI's crawler
accesses 1,700 pages for every one referral it sends back; Anthropic's ratio
is 73,000:1 [20]. Over 1 million Cloudflare customers have blocked AI crawlers
since July 2024 [20]. This creates a growing blind spot where high-quality
content is progressively excluded from AI-accessible sources.

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- **SEME applicability to agentic research:** The SEME studies [10][11]
  measure effects on human voting preferences. Whether LLM agents are
  similarly susceptible to ranking effects (rather than just humans reading
  ranked results) is not directly tested.
- **FAZE score interpretation:** The FAZE metric [9] measures favorability in
  generated descriptions, not necessarily in research synthesis. Whether
  geographic bias in descriptions translates to geographic bias in source
  selection for research is inferred, not demonstrated.
- **Source coverage snapshot:** The 37% domain divergence [5] and 84.9%
  uniqueness [45] are point-in-time measurements. Search engine behavior
  evolves rapidly, and these figures may shift as LLM-SEs mature.
- **Crawler blocking dynamics:** The 1M+ blocking figure [20] comes from
  Cloudflare, one CDN provider. The total blocking rate across all providers
  and self-hosted sites is unknown but likely higher.
- **Missing: recency bias quantification.** While recency bias in search is
  widely acknowledged, no cited study provides quantitative measures of how
  LLM retrieval systems weight recent vs older sources.
- **Missing: language bias in retrieval.** The geographic bias data [8][9]
  captures output bias but not whether retrieval itself is skewed toward
  English-language sources when researching non-English topics.

## 2026-04-18 Update

- **Geopolitical bias in LLM outputs [77]:** 4 LLMs, 4 languages, 55 historical conflicts. Substantial prejudice toward specific national narratives. Simple debiasing prompts have limited effect.
- **News-source concentration [78]:** AI Search Arena — 366,000+ citations, 24,000+ conversations. Citation concentration among a limited number of outlets. Pronounced liberal skew. User satisfaction NOT driven by political leaning or source quality — driven by response length alone.
- **Retrieval bias [79] (EACL 2026):** Retrieval systems favor frequently-retrieved claims, inflating metrics for popular content while under-representing low-frequency multilingual claims. Closes part of the "language bias in retrieval" gap flagged above.
- **Crawler-blocking ineffectiveness [80]:** 4M-citation analysis across ChatGPT/Gemini/Google. Sites blocking AI crawlers are still cited 70.6-92.3% of the time depending on bot variant. ~70% of ChatGPT citations come from sites blocking retrieval bots.
- **AI search does NOT reduce confirmation bias [121]:** 2.8M search results 2024-2025. AI search "speaks with one voice," shows lower response variety than traditional search, reinforces prior positions. Contradicts optimistic "LLM search aggregates diverse views" framing.
- **Crawler-to-referral ratios evolving [20 extended]:** Q1 2026 data shows ClaudeBot blocking grew 9.6%→10.1% of DISALLOW rules; ratios now differ materially from the 2025 Cloudflare baseline (ClaudeBot now 20,583:1 per Q1 2026 data vs. 73,000:1 in 2025 — flagged for methodology reconciliation).
